data.title: Lindblad acquires a controlling stake in a luxury Antarctic travel company
data.description:
Lindblad Expeditions Holdings (LIND) announced it has acquired a majority ownership of White Desert and Echo Charlie in the largest transaction in the company's history. A majority stake of 60% in White Desert and Echo Charlie was executed for an aggregate cash purchase price of approximately $61M, plus approximately $6M for cash on the balance sheet and subject to customary true-up adjustments for working capital, cash, and indebtedness. 

Established in 2005 by record-breaking polar explorer Patrick Woodhead, White Desert flies clients into the remote interior of Antarctica, blending logistical precision with a level of comfort previously unheard of on the ice. Billed as the ultimate bucket-list adventure, their itineraries include a journey to the geographic South Pole and a visit to an emperor penguin colony of over 20K birds.

The company said the strategic acquisition marks the beginning of an exciting new chapter in Antarctic travel. Leveraging their shared expertise, Lindblad Expeditions and White Desert see significant opportunities to expand White Desert's extraordinary offering through the development of camps and guest experiences. 

Through its global platform and expertise, Lindblad Expeditions (LIND) said it will also support the development and growth of a brand-new offering called Echo Charlie. "Inspired by the golden age of aviation aboard a fully restored DC-3 (an aircraft that can land on remote airstrips without the hassle of commercial airports), this new offering fuses real-life adventure with the seamless connection of highly diverse landscapes," highlighted Lindblad (LIND).

Like other companies that have joined the Lindblad family, White Desert and Echo Charlie will continue to operate as a stand-alone offering, preserving their founder-led vision and distinctive culture while benefiting from the reach, capabilities, and resources of Lindblad Expeditions.

Lindblad Expeditions (LIND) also raises its full-year 2026 revenue, net yield, and adjusted EBITDA guidance to reflect the acquisitions of White Desert and Echo Charlie, as well as continued strong performance across the business. The current expectations for the full year 2026 are fortour revenue of $850M to $880M, net yield per available guest night of 5.5% to 6.5%, and adjusted EBITDA of $140M to $148M.

Shares of Lindblad (LIND) were up 0.5% in premarket trading.

data.title: Profusa clears Nasdaq compliance issues
data.description:
• Profusa (PFSA) said it has regained compliance with Nasdaq’s minimum bid price and equity requirements.
  • However, it will remain subject to a one-year mandatory Nasdaq monitoring period. If it fails to meet the equity requirement during that period, Nasdaq can issue a delisting determination without first allowing the company to submit a compliance plan.
  • The stock price traded about 9.8% lower on Tuesday pre-market hours.

data.title: KKR, Neuberger units to take minority stake in Datavant
data.description:
Neuberger Capital Solutions, Neuberger Private Markets, and KKR (KKR) have agreed to acquire a minority stake in Datavant, the health data collaboration platform, alongside existing investor New Mountain Capital, the companies said on Tuesday.

New Mountain Capital, a Datavant investor since 2014, will retain its control position. The transaction is expected to close in 4Q 2026. Financial terms of the minority stake acquisition were not disclosed.

"With New Mountain, Neuberger, and KKR by our side, we're well equipped to deepen our impact across the healthcare ecosystem and accelerate into our next phase of growth," said Kyle Armbrester, CEO of Datavant.

KKR is investing in Datavant primarily through funds and accounts managed by its Strategic Investments Group. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026.

data.title: Rockwell Automation joins Anthropic’s Project Glasswing
data.description:
• Rockwell Automation (ROK) on Tuesday said it has joined Anthropic’s (ANTHRO) Project Glasswing, designed to advance AI-enabled cyber defense for industrial critical infrastructure.
  • Through controlled access to Claude Mythos 5, Rockwell security teams are exploring ways to accelerate the discovery, validation, prioritization, and remediation of vulnerabilities across software and connected systems that manufacturers rely on every day, the company said.

data.title: Axon announces proposed offering of $1B of 0% convertible senior notes
data.description:
• Axon Enterprise (AXON) on Tuesday said it intends to offer $1 billion aggregate principal amount of 0% convertible senior notes due 2031 in a public offering.

  • Axon also expects to grant the underwriters of the notes an option to purchase for settlement within an 11-day period beginning on, and including, the first date on which the notes are issued, up to an additional $150 million aggregate principal amount of notes, solely to cover over-allotments, if any.

 

  • Axon intends to use a portion of the net proceeds of the offering of the notes to pay the cost of the capped call transactions described below. Axon expects to use the remaining net proceeds for general corporate purposes.
  • The notes will mature on September 15, 2031, unless earlier converted, redeemed, or repurchased.
  • In connection with the pricing of the notes, Axon expects to enter into privately negotiated capped call transactions with one or more of the underwriters and/or their respective affiliates and/or other financial institutions.

data.title: Vera set for full FDA approval of Trutakna after late-stage trial win
data.description:
Vera Therapeutics (VERA) added more than 10% in premarket trading on Tuesday after announcing plans to seek full FDA approval for its lead asset Trutakna following a late-stage trial win in primary IgA nephropathy, an immune-mediated kidney disease.

The once-weekly injectable was approved in the U.S. in July under the FDA’s accelerated approval pathway to reduce proteinuria in adults with IgAN at risk of disease progression, with its continued availability subject to positive results in a confirmatory clinical trial.

Citing topline data from 428 adults with IgAN who were at risk for disease progression, the California-based biotech said on Tuesday that its Phase 3 ORIGIN 3 trial achieved all prespecified endpoints, including one related to estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR).

Based on the data, the company said it plans to submit a supplemental Biologics License Application in Q4 2026, seeking full FDA approval for Trutakna next year, noting that the drug has generated over 350 patient start forms during the first ten weeks of the launch.

“We are seeing paid claims and are pleased with initial payer policies. The early momentum of the TRUTAKNA launch is very encouraging,” Vera’s (VERA) chief commercial officer Matt Skelton said.

data.title: CareTrust REIT buys $400M skilled nursing portfolio, sees $600M pipeline
data.description:
• CareTrust REIT (CTRE) acquired a portfolio of skilled nursing facilities in the Southwest for $400M, expanding its investment activity as the healthcare REIT builds a sizable pipeline for the remainder of 2026.
  • The deal, which was effective September 1, was sourced off-market and completed through a joint venture in which CareTrust invested about $380M.
  • The portfolio is expected to generate a stabilized yield of approximately 8.6%. The acquisition brings CareTrust’s 2026 investment volume to $1.9B across 24 transactions, at a blended stabilized yield of about 8.7%.

data.title: Micron Taiwan union escalates profit-sharing push, keeps strike option open
data.description:
A potential strike at Micron Technology’s (MU) Taiwan operations is emerging as a new risk for the memory-chip maker, with a local union threatening industrial action over demands for a permanent employee profit-sharing plan.

The Taoyuan union, which represents workers at Micron’s facility in northern Taiwan, said it could call for a strike vote if the company fails to make meaningful progress in negotiations scheduled for Sept. 18 and 21.

"If there is no concrete proposal on September 18 and 21 and employees feel the company is simply dragging out the process, we will declare the negotiations have broken down and move towards a strike vote," said Jerry Lin, chairman of the Taoyuan union.

The standoff comes as Micron benefits from strong demand for memory chips used in artificial intelligence infrastructure. Taiwan is a major manufacturing base for the company’s DRAM and high-bandwidth memory products, making any disruption potentially significant for an already constrained market.

The union said it was seeking a permanent mechanism that would distribute 15% of Micron’s operating profit to employees worldwide. It has argued that one-time bonuses do not provide the transparency or long-term participation in company profits that workers are seeking.

Micron (MU) last week announced fiscal 2026 rewards for more than 60,000 employees globally, describing the period as an "extraordinary year" for the company. Eligible Taiwan employees who joined before Aug. 29, 2025, will receive a T$1M ($31,498) cash bonus, with later hires receiving prorated payments.

Workers’ representatives, however, said the bonus program fell short of their demands and criticized Micron for announcing the rewards while mediation was still in progress.

Micron did not directly respond to the union’s strike threat in an emailed response to Reuters. The company said: "We will continue listening to our ⁠team members’ perspectives and remain committed to engaging in the mediation process in good faith,"

The dispute comes as Taiwan unions seek to bring Micron’s compensation practices closer to those of Samsung Electronics (SSNLF) and SK Hynix (SKHY), both of which operate employee profit-sharing programs.

Further mediation is planned with the Taoyuan union and another union representing Micron employees in Taichung. The two groups collectively represent more than 80% of Micron’s approximately 15,000 employees in Taiwan, according to the Taoyuan union.

The Taoyuan union is also planning a worker event Thursday near Micron’s Hwa Ya Technology Park facility.
